title: KV TTL rotation & seqlen boundary exploration
content:
Personal scratchpad — KV TTL rotation + sequence-length edge tests
Owner: Aisha M. Patel
Context: trying to reproduce intermittent loss of context after ~8192-8220 tokens on rtx-gpu pool with kv_cache_v2 + flash_attn fallback. Similar to RW-2713 but different repro pattern (non-deterministic with batching).

Summary of the problem:
- Long-running chat sessions lose older tokens (responses start hallucinating as if prefix dropped).
- Observed after a TTL-based eviction run and when client sequence length jumps across a boundary (e.g., 4096 -> 8193).
- Suspect interplay between KV TTL rotation, per-shard kernel selection (flash_attn vs sparse_attn), and cache slot alignment when sequence lengths cross compile-time optim assumptions.

Repro steps attempted (local):
1) Start local inference with patched logger:
   $ ./server/bin/inference_server --conf configs/local-rt.conf --log-level debug --kv-ttl-check 60
2) Run synthetic client that appends tokens to push seqlen across thresholds:
   $ python tests/synthetic_client.py --model rwlm-13b --batch 1 --tokens-per-step 300 --steps 30
3) Watch metrics: /metrics (prom) and logs (stdout).

Commands / small hacks tried:
- Forcing kernel selection env var:
   $ export RW_FORCE_KERNEL=flash_attn
   $ ./server/bin/inference_server ...
- Forcing cache variant:
   $ export RW_KV_VARIANT=kv_cache_v1
- Recompiled with boundary checks in kv_index_rotate() and added assert in kv.c:
   if (new_index % cache_slots == 0) log_warn(...);
- Added a one-off fix: zero-pad kv slot metadata during rotate to ensure alignment:
   (quick patch) src/kv/rotate.c: memset(slot_meta+offset, 0, pad_bytes);

Observed behaviors (snippets):
- Kernel selection log around problematic window:
  [2025-01-20T14:02:12.241Z] kernel_select: model=rwlm-13b seq=8188 prefer=flash_attn selected=flash_attn
  [2025-01-20T14:02:12.313Z] kernel_select: model=rwlm-13b seq=8194 prefer=flash_attn selected=sparse_attn  <-- unexpected change

- KV rotate trace (simplified):
  rotate start idx=12288 epoch=5
  rotate end idx=16384 epoch=6
  kv_slot_align mismatch: expected_align=64 actual=56  <-- suspicious, alignment drift

- Error/stack when behavior reproduced:
  EPOCH=6: evicting slots 12288..16383
  E[14:02:12.315] kv_get: invalid slot header (magic mismatch) at slot=13200
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "server/worker.py", line 421, in handle_request
      out = runtime.generate(request)
    File "runtime/engine.py", line 128, in generate
      kv = self.kv_cache.get(prefix_id)
  RuntimeError: KV header checksum failed (expected 0x5a3f, got 0x0000)

Hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: When sequence length crosses the JITed-kernel threshold, the runtime switches kernel mid-stream and kernel-specific KV layout expectations differ, leading to misinterpreting slots (header magic mismatch).
- Hypothesis B: KV TTL rotation uses a chunk-aligned rotation size; under certain batch/sequence combos the padding is not applied, producing header truncation (observed align mismatch 64 vs 56).
- Hypothesis C: Cache slot metadata written by background rotating thread races with inference threads reading slots when kernel choice changes buffer sizes (race exacerbated by continuous-batching).

Quick experiments to validate hypotheses:
- Force stable kernel across boundary (RW_FORCE_KERNEL=flash_attn) — reduces incidence drastically (went from ~1/50 to 0/200 runs). Supports Hyp A/C.
- Increased kv-rotation mutex granularity (coarse lock) — reduced rate but increased latency. Suggests race in C.
- Added zero-padding on rotation — reduced header checksum failures but not fully eliminated (likely partial overlap window).

Micro-repro script (used locally):
- tests/repro/kv-seqlen-edge.py (rough):
  * warmup 20k tokens to populate cache
  * concurrently spin 4 clients, drop one client into seq=8194 on step boundary
  * sleep 0.01 between token sends to simulate real user pacing
  * re-run with RW_FORCE_KERNEL env var toggles

Next steps / TODOs:
- Add kernel-compatibility metadata to KV slot header (version + kernel_mask) so mismatch is detectable and graceful fallback triggered.
- Add per-slot write fences when rotation writes header (small perf hit but quick to test).
- Create a targeted unit test that simulates mid-rotation read of header (C-level test harness).
- Collect full core dumps / memory map when checksum mismatch occurs (need SRE help to attach gdb on node).
- Share findings in RW-2713 and schedule 1-hr debug sesh with Ravi + Marisol.

Notes / stray observations:
- The mismatch often shows up when a client does an immediate big jump (e.g., imported conversation appended all at once). Sequential incremental appends less likely to trigger.
- CPU affinity of rotation thread seems to drift to different socket under load; I saw more failures when rotation thread ran on socket 1 and inference on socket 0 (possible NUMA effect).

Raw kernel selection debug log (context window compressed):
  [14:02:11.987] batch=3 seq=4096 candidate_kernels=[flash_attn,sparse_attn] choose=flash_attn
  [14:02:12.310] batch=3 seq=8194 candidate_kernels=[flash_attn,sparse_attn] choose=sparse_attn  # fallback path picked due to failed fast-path init

Attached quick links: RW-2713 (jira), PR#6789 (runtime kv fixes), slack thread thread5678 (chat excerpts).

If I had to prioritize: 1) add write-fence+slot-version header (fast mitigation), 2) force stable kernel selection until header versioning is in place, 3) add unit test and SRE assisted core capture.

End of scratchpad.
